findings.reason: the §8 node would perform the stated move, run the trace, find crew-home opens it cannot remove, and have to decide outside the plan whether the producer-lease renewal moves into the station (a §7 mechanism §7 does not state) or the producers retire early (contradicting §7's "retires nothing immediately" and §12's measured cutover); the trace measure as written is unsatisfiable by the mechanism the section describes.
findings.text: §8 asserts the follower "reads nothing on GPFS" and measures "a 60 s `strace -f -e trace=openat,stat,newfstatat` of a running subscriber names no path under the crew home", but the follower's per-wait pass calls `_renew_producer_lease()` (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1760`), which opens `crew_home()/watch/<project>-<digest>.lock` at least twice on every pass through `runs.renew_producer_lease` → `producer_live` (`reckon/crew/runs.py:3064`) and `watch_lease_renewed_at` → `read_watch_registration` (`reckon/crew/runs.py:2071-2085`), and writes its own delivery lease under `runs.follower_dir` (`reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:66`) — §8 moves only the registration, checkpoint and history, and §7 keeps the per-project producers running beside the station until §12's cutover so the renewal is still required (a producer ends one lease interval after the last renewal)

findings.reason: the write lands inside a 60 s window whenever a row is drawn, so the control is satisfiable as intended; naming the per-pass access would sharpen it but does not change what the node builds.
